The video segment opens with a title card reading "How to Format an APA Style Paper using Word for Mac," followed by the author's name, "Terrence D. Jorgensen," and his affiliation, "Kennesaw State University," all in green text against a black background. The screen then transitions to a visual of the cover of the sixth edition of the "Publication Manual of the American Psychological Association," displaying the title and the organization's name. A Mac OS X desktop appears, showing the system information window against a dark background. Then the video then shows a blank Microsoft Word document. The narrator moves the word document around the screen and adjusts the zoom, demonstrating the use of the operating system. Finally, the text from the book cover is overlayed on top of the word document.

Here is a description of the video segment:

The video shows a person demonstrating how to format a references page in Microsoft Word. The person is not visible, but the actions in the Word document are clear. The document contains text like “ALL CAPS” and “Title: Subtitle” on the first page, followed by a blank second page. To create a page break for the references page, the person clicks on "Insert", then "Break", then "Section Break (Next Page)". The word "References" is typed at the top of the new page, and centered using the toolbar. The person removes any indentation, then moves the cursor back to the left, and explains that the references must be set with a hanging indentation. This can be done with the ruler at the top of the text. Alternatively, it can be done by going back to the "Format" menu, then "Paragraph", and setting the indentation to "hanging." A sample reference entry is placed in the document. The demonstrator states that the APA manual can be consulted for more details about formatting the references.
